title: FACT CHECK: Suan did not propose parliamentary gov’t if VP Sara isn’t impeached
summary: The Cagayan de Oro Press Club also debunked the claim, saying the congressman never made the remarks shown in the altered videos circulating online

blocks.text: Claim: A video shows Cagayan de Oro 1st District Representative Lordan Suan saying that if Vice President Sara Duterte is not impeached, the law should be changed to shift the Philippines into a parliamentary form of government with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as prime minister.
Why we fact-checked this: Multiple trending posts used a clip of Suan delivering a speech during the Cagayan de Oro Press Club’s 75th Anniversary Gala on November 23.

The video shows Suan supposedly saying, “Kung hindi man ma-impeach si Sara, gumawa na lang tayo ng batas para walang election sa 2028. (If [Vice President] Sara [Duterte] is not impeached, let’s just enact a law to cancel the 2028 elections.) Let’s transform the Philippines into a parliamentary form of government so that President Bongbong Marcos can become prime minister.”
A Facebook page called Defense Lawyers, one of the accounts that posted the video, wrote this as a caption: “Ano daw? BBM as Prime Minister?!!” (Say what? BBM as prime minister?)
The post garnered 11,700 reactions, 4,700 comments, and 1,700 shares as of writing.
Facebook user Amy Ugay also posted a vertical version of the video with a text overlay that says, “Oi Suan ikaw na lang kaya mag prime minister bakit si BBM pa tigilan mo ‘yan kahibangan mo.”
(Hey Suan, why don’t you just become prime minister yourself instead of BBM? Stop this nonsense of yours.)
This post had 2,000 reactions, 742 comments, and 301 shares as of writing.
The facts: The audio used in the video is fake – Suan did not make any statement regarding Duterte, Marcos, or scrapping the elections in 2028.

A video shared by iFM CDO radio station showed Suan’s speech at the event, where he discussed the importance of the press amid widespread misinformation. He also mentioned House Bill No. 9397, or the proposed Right to Information Act, which seeks to institutionalize Filipinos’ right to access information on matters of public concern.
During his four-minute speech, Suan did not mention anything about the elections, Duterte’s impeachment, or proposing the country’s transition to a parliamentary form of government.

Suan’s office also categorically denied the claims, saying in a statement to Rappler on November 27 that the lawmaker remains an advocate of democracy and upholds Filipinos’ right to vote and choose their leaders.
His office added: “Walang puwang sa ating demokrasya ang sinadyang pagpapakalat ng kasinungalingan upang linlangin ang taumbayan.”
(There is no place in our democracy for the deliberate spreading of lies to deceive the public.)

The Cagayan de Oro Press Club refuted the false claims in a Facebook statement published on November 26, clarifying that the congressman joined the event to show solidarity with local journalists and that he never uttered those statements.
“We call on vloggers and netizens to stop spreading unverified information that confuses the public and damages the reputation of our guests,” the statement read further.
